tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Where a first-time user gets stuck

I walked JusPrin’s first launch on every path I could reach and found 23 places a newcomer is likely to misread or stall. Each orange number marks the spot on the screenshot; the same number below says what is on screen, why it confuses, and a proposed fix.

The proposals are mine and nothing is decided. The app freeze after Import is left out because another session is fixing it.

The welcome screen

  1. 1

    The only buttons are “Continue with Google” and “Continue with email”. The line under them says “New or existing account, same door.”

    A new person looks for “Sign up” or “Create account” and finds neither, so they wonder whether they need an account from somewhere else first. You flagged this one.

    ProposalLead with signing up: the email button reads “Sign up free”, with a small “Already have an account? Sign in” link under it. Both still send the same email code; only the words change.

  2. 2

    Above the three boxes: “Pick how the agent should think. Change it any time in Preferences › Agent.”

    The boxes are three ways to pay for or connect the agent, not ways of thinking. The person doesn’t know yet what the agent is, what Preferences is, or why they must choose now.

    ProposalSay what the choice is: “Sign up to use the AI agent, or skip it and just slice.”

  3. 3

    “An Expert message is 5 credits.”

    “Expert” appears nowhere else on the screen, so the person can’t tell what 500 credits buys.

    ProposalSay it in things the person does, for example “500 credits is about 100 questions to the agent”. The number needs checking against real costs.

  4. 4

    “Your own API key — Free” and “Claude Code or Claude Desktop — Free · MCP server”.

    “API key” and “MCP server” are developer words. “Free” beside them makes the 500-credit offer look like the expensive choice, and an API key isn’t free: the person pays the AI company directly.

    ProposalFold both into one quieter link, “Use your own AI account instead”, and explain the two options on the screen it opens.

Signing in with email

  1. 5

    The card asks “How do you want to sign in?” and offers a Password box with “Forgot password”. The line that tells a new person what to do, “New here? The code makes your account.”, is the smallest text on the card.

    A new person has no password. A password box suggests they should already have one.

    ProposalShow only “Email me a 6-digit code” at first, with a small “Use a password instead” link for people who set one.

Typing the emailed code

  1. 6

    “The sixth digit signs you in. Read the email on any device.”

    It reads like a riddle. It means the app signs you in as soon as you type the last digit, and you can open the email on your phone.

    Proposal“Type the code from the email. You can open it on your phone.”

  2. 7

    “Use the browser instead”.

    Nothing says what happens in the browser. It means “sign in with Google instead”.

    Proposal“Sign in with Google instead”.

Waiting for Google

  1. 8

    “Finish signing in in your browser.”

    The doubled “in” reads as a typo.

    Proposal“Finish in your browser.”

The printer step, signed in

  1. 9

    “Signed in as new@example.com · 500 credits”. Your screenshot showed the same line on the OrcaSlicer import screen.

    The person just got 500 credits, and the line doesn’t say so. “500 credits” after a dot reads like a balance they had before. You flagged this one.

    Proposal“You got 500 free credits for signing up.” with the email address on a smaller line under it.

  2. 10

    “OrcaSlicer printers in another folder? Choose the folder…”

    It shows to everyone the app found no OrcaSlicer folder for, which includes everyone who has never used OrcaSlicer.

    ProposalRemove it here. The File › Import › “Import from OrcaSlicer…” menu item covers this later, once it is built.

  3. 11

    “Skip, and JusPrin slices for a generic 0.4 mm printer until you add yours.” The code shows that Skip installs OrcaSlicer’s “Generic Klipper Printer”: a 250 × 250 mm bed and Klipper G-code.

    A Bambu or Prusa owner who skips gets G-code that may not run on their printer or fit their bed, and nothing says so.

    ProposalSay what the stand-in is: “Until you add yours, files are sliced for a 250 mm Klipper printer and may not print on other printers.”

Choosing a printer model

  1. 12

    After the model is chosen, Continue stays grey and nothing on screen says why. In my run it stayed grey for 84 seconds while the app read the printer’s filaments and plates in the background.

    The person thinks they missed a field, or that the app is broken. The Mac was heavily loaded by other builds at the time (load 21 on 12 cores), so a normal Mac is probably faster; I didn’t measure that.

    ProposalShow “Reading this printer’s settings…” with a spinner under the nozzle buttons while Continue waits.

Bringing printers from OrcaSlicer

  1. 13

    All eight printers come over together. There is no way to leave one out.

    People keep old printers in OrcaSlicer that they no longer own, and they all show up in JusPrin.

    ProposalA tick box per printer, all ticked to start.

  2. 14

    The screen doesn’t say which printer JusPrin will use after the import.

    With eight printers, the person can’t guess which one their next slice uses.

    Proposal“JusPrin starts with Bambu Lab P1S, the printer OrcaSlicer had selected.”

  3. 15

    “Start fresh”.

    It sounds like it erases something. It means “skip the import and pick my printer by hand”.

    Proposal“Choose my printer instead”.

  4. 16

    The folder path and “· 3 filaments” share one line, and the count breaks onto two lines at the far right.

    The count is easy to miss and the path means nothing to most people.

    Proposal“Also brings 3 filaments” on its own line, and the path in smaller text.

What the import brought

  1. 17

    One filament failed out of seven items, and the title says “Some settings need attention”.

    It sounds alarming, and it calls printers and filaments “settings”.

    Proposal“Imported from OrcaSlicer” as the title, with the one failure shown in its row.

  2. 18

    “Not imported · its base profile, Kingroon PLA Silk, isn’t in JusPrin”, and a “Retry failed items” button.

    “Base profile” is jargon, there is no next step, and Retry fails the same way for this reason.

    Proposal“This filament is built on Kingroon PLA Silk, which JusPrin doesn’t have.” Show Retry only for failures a retry can fix, such as a file that couldn’t be read.

  3. 19

    “OrcaSlicer’s own files were not changed.”

    It answers a worry nobody raised here. The screen before already said “OrcaSlicer keeps its own copy.”

    ProposalRemove it.

Home, not signed in

  1. 20

    The printer added a moment ago says “Not connected. No network connection is set up.”

    It reads like something went wrong while adding it.

    Proposal“Connect it to send prints straight from JusPrin” beside the Connect button, with no status word until a connection was tried.

  2. 21

    The “Set up the agent” card repeats the sign-in card but never says what the agent does or that signing up gives 500 credits.

    Someone who skipped the welcome has no reason to fill it in.

    ProposalOne line of why at the top: “Get 500 free credits and ask the agent to fix failed prints.”

Home, signed in

  1. 22

    The same 500 credits have three names: “Your first month: 500 credits” on the welcome, “500 credits” after signing in, and “First-month credits … Expires 4 Dec” here. The expiry date first appears on Home.

    People wonder whether these are different credits, and learn they expire only after signing up.

    ProposalOne name everywhere, and the expiry in the sign-up line: “You got 500 free credits, good until 4 December.”

  2. 23

    “JusPrin account · Connected”, above a printer that says “Not connected”.

    “Connected” is printer language. For an account it reads as if the account is linked to a device.

    Proposal“Signed in as new@example.com”.

How this was checked

  • A scratch copy of the current build ran with its own empty data folder and a copy of your OrcaSlicer folder. The welcome, the printer form, the OrcaSlicer list and Home after adding a printer are the real app.
  • Sign-in screens, signed-in screens and the import result are the real page with the app’s state set by hand. I didn’t create accounts on staging or run the import.
  • Not covered: native windows and menus, such as Preferences (opened by “Your own API key”), the folder chooser and OrcaSlicer’s own dialogs, because screen control wasn’t available.
  • Also seen, not a wording problem: pressing Continue on the printer step froze the app for about 108 seconds while it installed the printer. That looks like the same kind of freeze as the one after Import.

content.text:
Yes. The first-launch text was written by someone who already knew how everything worked, so it squeezes each mechanism into a few clever words. A newcomer has to rebuild the meaning from those words, and usually can't. It's the same habit your global CLAUDE.md warns against: packing a mechanism into a short phrase instead of saying what the person does and what happens.

Here are the clearest cases from the review, with the original first and the proposal second.

**"New or existing account, same door."**
This is a metaphor standing in for a fact. What it means is that the same button works whether or not you have an account, and creates one if you don't. The reader has to work out what "door" refers to.
Proposal: a "Sign up free" button with "Already have an account? Sign in" under it. A new person sees the words they were looking for and doesn't have to decode anything.

**"The sixth digit signs you in. Read the email on any device."**
This describes how the code box works on the inside: it submits when the last digit is typed. It doesn't tell the person what to do.
Proposal: "Type the code from the email. You can open it on your phone." That gives one action, and "any device" becomes a concrete one.

**"New here? The code makes your account."**
This one's compressed into a cause and effect: the code creates the account. And the one line a new person needs is the smallest text on the card.
Proposal: show only "Email me a 6-digit code" at first, so there's no password box asking them for something they don't have.

**"Pick how the agent should think."**
This metaphor hides what the choice really is: how to pay for or connect the AI.
Proposal: "Sign up to use the AI agent, or skip it and just slice." It names both options and what each one means.

**"Signed in as new@example.com · 500 credits"**
The middle dot joins two facts and drops how they relate, so "500 credits" reads like a balance the person already had.
Proposal: "You got 500 free credits for signing up." The relationship is spelled out.

**"Skip, and JusPrin slices for a generic 0.4 mm printer until you add yours."**
This one's dense in a different way: it leaves out the consequence. "Generic" hides the fact that the app sets up a 250 mm Klipper printer.
Proposal: "files are sliced for a 250 mm Klipper printer and may not print on other printers." It says what will actually happen to the person's files.

**"Not imported · its base profile, Kingroon PLA Silk, isn't in JusPrin"**
These are fragments joined by a dot, around a piece of jargon ("base profile").
Proposal: "This filament is built on Kingroon PLA Silk, which JusPrin doesn't have." It's a complete sentence in everyday words.

**"An Expert message is 5 credits."**
"Expert" is an internal label that appears nowhere else on the screen.
Proposal: describe the cost in things the person does, like "about 100 questions to the agent".

All the rewrites follow the same few moves. Each one uses full sentences instead of fragments joined by dots. It names the thing the person does, not how the system works inside. It spells out the consequence instead of hinting at it. And it uses words a newcomer already has.

One caveat: the rewrites haven't been tried on real users. When I say they're clearer, that's my judgment from reading them, not a measured result.

lastPrompt: I found that the design agents has a very strong tendency to spell out cryptic messages on the user interface. What would be a good way to counter that?

content.text:
Today the project has almost nothing guarding the text people see on screen. `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` has one line about it ("use plain language instead of slicer jargon where possible"). The wording tests in `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` only check text the model reads, never the text a person reads.

**Why I think it happens.** This is my explanation, not something I've tested. The agent writing the screen knows how it works, so "The sixth digit signs you in" reads clearly to it. UI space is tight, and short phrases look polished, so the agent keeps squeezing. Then whoever reviews it, often another agent with the same knowledge, finds it clear too. A rule like "use plain language" doesn't stop this, because the writer honestly believes it already wrote plainly. So the check has to come from someone who doesn't know how the screen works.

**What I'd do, strongest first:**

1. **A cold-reader check before a screen counts as done.** Hand a fresh agent only the screenshot: no code, no spec, no chat history. For each piece of text and each button, it says in its own words what it means and what will happen if it's pressed. Then compare that with what the screen is meant to do. Any mismatch means a rewrite, and you check again. That's basically how the first-launch review found its 23 problems, so it already works in practice. It catches exactly what the writer can't see.

2. **A wording rule with real before-and-after pairs** in the "Writing UI code" section of `design-system.md`, which every UI change already has to follow. Examples teach better than principles, so use pairs from the review. Name the five patterns behind them:
   - Two facts joined by a middle dot ("Signed in as … · 500 credits").
   - Metaphors ("same door", "how the agent should think").
   - Describing how the system works instead of what the person does ("The sixth digit signs you in").
   - Internal labels ("Expert").
   - Hinting at a consequence instead of stating it ("a generic 0.4 mm printer").

   The rule itself: every line says what the person does or what happens to them, in a full sentence, in words a newcomer already has.

3. **A small automated check as a backstop.** It would flag a middle dot joining clauses, plus a short list of jargon ("API key", "MCP", "base profile"), in the Home and Agent page text. It only catches surface patterns. It can't tell that a sentence is a riddle, so it supports the first two and doesn't replace them.

These are proposals. None of them is in the repo, and I haven't measured whether they cut down on cryptic text.

content.text:
No, I don't mean a person. I mean one extra agent step inside the design workflow you already run. When a design agent finishes a screen, a second agent that has never seen the code or the spec gets only the screenshot. It has to say what each line means and what each button will do. Wherever its answer differs from what the screen is meant to do, the text gets rewritten. That costs one subagent call per screen, not a new hire.

There's one honest caveat. My guess is that an agent is a weaker cold reader than a real newcomer. Models are good at decoding compressed text, so it might understand "The sixth digit signs you in" even though a person stalls on it. I haven't tested that. So the agent check would be a cheap filter, and a real first-time user would stay the final test for the screens that matter most, like first launch.

We can find out whether the agent check is good enough. I'd run a fresh agent, as the cold reader, on the original first-launch screenshots from the review and count how many of the 23 problems it catches. If it catches most of them, the step is worth adding to the design workflow. If it misses many, it isn't, and we'd need a person after all. Want me to run that test?

input.prompt:
You are playing a first-time user of a desktop app. You know nothing about how it was built. Your job is to read ten screenshots of the app's first launch and say, honestly, what you understand and where you'd hesitate.

Background, which is all a real new user would know: you own a 3D printer and just installed JusPrin, a desktop app that prepares 3D models for printing (a "slicer"). You've opened it for the first time. The screenshots are in the order you'd meet them:

/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/e017b21e-f4da-471a-9b19-14e9148b503c/scratchpad/coldread/screens/screen-01.jpg through screen-10.jpg

Rules:
- Read ONLY those ten image files with the Read tool. Do not open any other file, directory, repository, web page or artifact, and do not search for anything. Using anything beyond the pictures would spoil the test.
- Read the text in the pictures literally, the way a busy newcomer would. Don't be generous: if you have to puzzle out what a line means, that counts as a problem even if you eventually work it out.
- Do not stop partway to ask questions or wait for anything; finish all ten screens in one go.

For each screen, write:
1. Every line of text and every button or link, quoted exactly, each followed by one plain sentence saying what you think it means, or for a button what you expect will happen when you press it. If you're unsure, say so and give your best guess.
2. "Where I'd hesitate": each spot that would make you stop, misread, worry, or not know what to do next. Quote the words (or describe the missing information), say what you'd likely think or do, and why. Include things the screen fails to tell you that you'd want to know at that moment.

End with a short list of the problems you'd fix first across all screens, most harmful first.

Plain prose, no tables. Be specific and quote exactly.

<result>I read all ten screens in order, as someone who owns a printer, has just installed JusPrin and knows nothing else.

## Screen 1: welcome and sign-in

**What each line says to me**

- **"JusPrin"** with an ice-cream logo: the app's name. The ice cream doesn't suggest printing to me, but it's harmless.
- **The pictures:** a clean green boat on a grid next to a photo of a stringy, failed blue-and-white boat. I take it to mean "it turns the bad print into the good one."
- **"▶ Photo credits":** opens who took the photos. I'd ignore it.
- **"The AI slicer that fixes failed prints.":** this is a slicer with AI that fixes prints that went wrong. That's clear.
- **"Show it a photo of what went wrong. The agent reads your file, your settings and your slice, changes the settings and slices again.":** I photograph a failed print, and something called "the agent" changes my settings and re-slices. "The agent" is introduced without saying what it is. I guess it's the AI.
- **"Pick how the agent should think. Change it any time in Preferences › Agent.":** I'm being asked to choose how the AI thinks. But none of the choices below are about thinking. They're about accounts and payment.
- **"Your first month: 500 credits":** signing up gives me 500 free credits for a month.
- **"An Expert message is 5 credits. Your own API key stays free.":** some messages cost 5 credits. I don't know what an "Expert message" is, whether there are cheaper ones, or what an API key is for here.
- **"Continue with Google":** signs me in with my Google account.
- **"or":** a divider between Google and email.
- **"you@example.com"** field: I type my email here.
- **"Continue with email"** (greyed out): sign in with my email once I've typed it.
- **"New or existing account, same door. Google opens your browser; email stays here.":** I had to read it twice. I think it means the same button works whether or not I have an account, Google sign-in opens a browser, and email sign-in stays inside the app.
- **"By signing in you agree to the Terms and Privacy Policy.":** the usual legal line, with links.
- **"Your own API key"** with "Free": use my own AI key instead of credits. I'm guessing it means an OpenAI-type key. It doesn't say.
- **"Claude Code or Claude Desktop"** with "Free · MCP server": no idea. Something for people who use Claude. "MCP server" means nothing to me.
- **"Just slice for now":** skip all of this and use it as a normal slicer.

**Where I'd hesitate**

- **"Pick how the agent should think."** I'd look for options about thinking style, like fast versus careful, and find sign-in boxes instead. That makes me doubt I'm reading the page right.
- **"Your first month: 500 credits."** My first worry is what happens after the month. Do I get charged automatically? Do I need a card? Nothing says whether it's free to sign up or what it costs later, so I'd hesitate before handing over my email.
- **"An Expert message is 5 credits."** I can't tell how far 500 credits goes. Is that 100 messages? Is one failed-print fix one message or twenty?
- **"Your own API key stays free."** Free compared to what? "API key" is developer jargon, and I don't know which company's key it wants.
- **"Claude Code or Claude Desktop · Free · MCP server."** This is jargon aimed at a different audience. It makes the page feel like it isn't for me.
- **"New or existing account, same door."** The odd phrasing slows me down.
- **"Just slice for now"** is small and sits at the bottom. If I'm cautious about accounts, I'd struggle to see that skipping is a normal choice. I'd also wonder whether I could still use the AI later without signing in now.

## Screen 2: after entering my email

**What each line says to me**

- The headline, description and "Pick how the agent should think" line are the same as before.
- **"How do you want to sign in?":** it's asking whether I want a code or a password.
- **"alex@example.com. Change email":** the email I typed, with a link to fix it.
- **"Email me a 6-digit code"** (main button): sends a code to my inbox.
- **"New here? The code makes your account.":** if I'm new, using the code creates my account.
- **"or"**
- **"Password"** field with **"Sign in"**: if I already have a password, I type it here.
- **"Forgot password":** the reset flow.
- **"Cancel":** go back to screen 1.
- "Your own API key", "Claude Code or Claude Desktop" and "Just slice for now" are unchanged.

**Where I'd hesitate**

- The password box appears even though I'm new and never made a password. For a moment I'd wonder whether I already have an account, maybe from an older JusPrin or Obico. It's fine once I read "New here?", but showing a password field to a brand-new email feels like I'm missing something.
- Nothing says whether choosing the code means I'll have no password later. Would I need a code every time?

## Screen 3: entering the code

**What each line says to me**

- **"Check your email.":** go to my inbox.
- **"We sent a 6-digit code to alex@example.com.":** a code is on its way to that address.
- **Six boxes:** I type the code one digit per box.
- **"The sixth digit signs you in.":** I think it means that when I type the last digit, it signs me in automatically with no button. That's a strange way to say it, and I had to work it out.
- **"Read the email on any device.":** I can check the email on my phone. Fine.
- **"Send a new code":** resends the code.
- **"Change email":** go back and fix my address.
- **"Use the browser instead":** I'm not sure. It might open a web page to sign in, or it might mean clicking a link in the email instead of typing the code. My best guess is that it opens the browser for a link-style sign-in.
- **"Cancel":** back to the start.

**Where I'd hesitate**

- **"The sixth digit signs you in."** It reads like a riddle. I might type five digits and look around for a Submit button.
- **"Use the browser instead"** is unclear. I wouldn't know whether it means Google or something else, so I'd avoid it.
- The screen doesn't say how long the code lasts, or to check my spam folder if nothing arrives. Those are the two things I'd wonder about while waiting.

## Screen 4: finishing sign-in in the browser

**What each line says to me**

- **Spinning arrows with "Finish signing in in your browser.":** a browser opened (Google, I assume), and I finish there. The "in in" reads like a typo.
- **"The app continues on its own once the browser is done.":** I don't need to click anything here afterwards.
- **"Nothing happened? Open the browser again":** reopens the browser if it didn't appear.
- **"Use an email code instead":** switch to the code method.
- **"Cancel":** stop signing in.

**Where I'd hesitate**

- **"in in"** looks like a mistake, but it's minor.
- When I'm in the browser, I don't know what to do when it says I'm done. Do I close the tab? Switch back to the app myself? The screen says the app continues on its own, but not whether I need to come back to it.

## Screen 5: which printer do I have (loading)

**What each line says to me**

- **"✓ Signed in as new@example.com · 500 credits":** I'm signed in and have 500 credits.
- **"Which printer do you have?":** pick my printer.
- **"JusPrin plans every print for your printer: its bed, its nozzle and the filament it starts with. You can add more printers later.":** it needs my printer to set things up properly, and I can add more later.
- **"Reading the printer list…":** it's loading the list of printers.
- **"Continue"** (greyed out): go on once I've chosen.
- **"Skip for now":** don't pick a printer yet.
- **"Skip, and JusPrin slices for a generic 0.4 mm printer until you add yours.":** if I skip, it uses a generic printer.
- **"OrcaSlicer printers in another folder? Choose the folder…":** if I used OrcaSlicer, I can point to where its printers are stored.
- **"Back":** goes back. To sign-in? I'm already signed in, so I'm not sure what Back would undo.

**Where I'd hesitate**

- The email says **new@example.com**, but I typed alex@example.com two screens ago. A real user who saw this would panic that they're signed into someone else's account. (This may be an artifact of how the screenshots were taken, but as a reader of the pictures I noticed it.)
- **"OrcaSlicer printers in another folder?"** If I never used OrcaSlicer, I don't know what it is. If I did, I'd wonder why my printers would be "in another folder" and how I'd know which folder that is.
- **"Back"** after a finished sign-in: I worry it signs me out.
- **"the filament it starts with"** promises a filament choice. I'd expect to be asked about filament next.

## Screen 6: printer chosen

**What each line says to me**

- The same headline and description.
- **"Brand": "Bambu Lab":** I picked my printer's maker.
- **"Model": "A1 mini":** I picked my model.
- **"Nozzle": "0.2 mm", "0.4 mm" (selected), "0.6 mm", "0.8 mm":** my nozzle size, with 0.4 chosen.
- **"Most printers ship with 0.4 mm.":** if I'm unsure, 0.4 is the safe choice. Helpful.
- **"Continue":** save this printer and move on.
- **"Skip for now"**, the generic-printer note and **"Back":** the same as before.

**Where I'd hesitate**

- **Continue still looks greyed out**, the same disabled style as on the loading screen, even though brand, model and nozzle are all filled in. I'd think I missed a required field and look for one, maybe the filament it mentioned. This is the biggest blocker on this screen. If it really is disabled, I'm stuck. If it's enabled but looks disabled, I'd still hesitate.
- The text says JusPrin plans for "the filament it starts with", but there's no filament question. Does it pick one for me, and which one?
- The "Signed in as… · 500 credits" line from the previous screen is gone. That's minor, but I'd wonder whether something reset.

## Screen 7: bring printers from OrcaSlicer

**What each line says to me**

- **"Bring your printers from OrcaSlicer?":** it found OrcaSlicer printers on my computer and offers to copy them.
- **"JusPrin copies these printers with their filaments, settings and printer connections. OrcaSlicer keeps its own copy.":** it copies them and doesn't touch OrcaSlicer. That's reassuring.
- **The list:** "Creality Ender-3 V2 Neo 0.4 nozzle - Copy", "Elegoo Neptune 3 Pro 0.4 nozzle - Copy", "Qidi X-Plus 4 0.4 nozzle - Copy", "Anycubic Kobra 3 0.4 nozzle", "Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle", "Creality K1C 0.4 nozzle", "MyKlipper 0.6 nozzle", "Bambu Lab P1S 0.4 nozzle". These are the eight printers it will copy.
- **"/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/473348c5-… · 3 filaments":** where it found them, and that there are 3 filaments.
- **"Import":** copy all eight.
- **"Start fresh":** don't copy anything.
- **"Back":** return to the printer picker.

**Where I'd hesitate**

- **The order is backwards.** I just picked my A1 mini by hand, and now I'm offered an A1 mini again. Will importing give me two A1 minis? Did my choice on the last screen count?
- **I can't choose which printers to bring.** There are no checkboxes. Most people have one or two printers, not eight. I'd hesitate to import all of them, including ones named "- Copy" that look like leftovers.
- **"Start fresh"** sounds like it might also throw away the printer I just picked, or wipe something. "Don't import" or "Skip" would be clearer.
- **The folder path** is long, cut off, and looks like an internal temporary or developer folder ("/private/tmp/claude/…"). It doesn't look like OrcaSlicer's real folder. I'd worry it's reading the wrong place.
- **"3 filaments"** is tucked at the end of the path line, oddly wrapped, with no list. Eight printers but only 3 filaments seems odd, and I can't see which ones.
- It doesn't say what "printer connections" means: network access to my printers? Passwords? I'd want to know before copying them.

## Screen 8: import results

**What each line says to me**

- **"Some settings need attention":** something went wrong with part of the import.
- **"OrcaSlicer's own files were not changed.":** my OrcaSlicer is safe.
- **"Creality Ender-3 V2 Neo 0.4 nozzle - Copy · Imported", "Elegoo Neptune 3 Pro 0.4 nozzle - Copy · Imported", "Qidi X-Plus 4 0.4 nozzle - Copy · Imported", "Bambu Lab P1S 0.4 nozzle · Imported":** these four copied fine.
- **"⚠ Kingroon PLA Silk @Qidi X-Plus 4 0.4 nozzle · Not imported · its base profile, Kingroon PLA Silk, isn't in JusPrin":** one filament couldn't be copied because something it depends on is missing.
- **"2 of 3 filaments imported":** two filaments worked and one didn't.
- **"Continue":** move on.
- **"Retry failed items":** try the failed one again.

**Where I'd hesitate**

- **Four of the eight printers are missing.** Anycubic Kobra 3, Bambu Lab A1 mini, Creality K1C and MyKlipper aren't listed at all: not imported, not failed, just gone. I'd assume they silently failed or were skipped, and I'd want to know why.
- **"Some settings need attention"** promises I can do something, but the only problem shown has no action except Retry. "Its base profile… isn't in JusPrin" is jargon. I don't know what a base profile is or how to add one.

Misses needed knowledge off the screen (Skip installs a Klipper printer) or subtler judgment (redundant reassurance, "Connected" for an account, one credit allowance under three names). It also raised real new questions (what happens after the free month, unlabeled × on the account card).

Kenneth's concern behind it: design agents strongly tend to write cryptic UI text.

**Why:** the writer knows the mechanism, so its own compressed text reads clear to it; only a reader without that context sees the problem.

**How to apply:** feed the cold reader screenshots from ONE coherent path. Mixing signed-in and not-signed-in screens, or hand-set states, produced false alarms (account email changing, "asked to sign in again", imported printers vanishing). Not yet adopted as a rule in design-system.md; see [[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]].

content.text:
The cold-reader test worked well for the problem you raised. The fresh agent saw only the 10 screenshots plus one line ("you own a 3D printer and just installed JusPrin"). It found 14 of the review's 23 problems outright and 4 more in part, and it caught every case of cryptic wording.

**Problems it caught by itself:**
- "Pick how the agent should think": it went looking for thinking options and found sign-in boxes.
- "Expert message", "API key" and "MCP server": it couldn't tell what 500 credits buys, and said the jargon "makes the page feel like it isn't for me."
- "Same door": "I had to read it twice."
- "The sixth digit signs you in": it called this a riddle and said it might type five digits and then look for a Submit button.
- "Use the browser instead": it couldn't tell whether this meant Google.
- "Signing in in": it read it as a typo.
- The password box for a new email, Continue staying grey with no reason, no way to leave printers out of the import, "Start fresh" sounding destructive, the path and filament count squeezed onto one line, "base profile" and a Retry that can't help, and "Not connected" looking like an error.

**Caught in part:** the missing "Sign up" button (it flagged the wording but didn't ask for the button), which printer gets used after the import, the alarming "Some settings need attention", and the free credits (it asked about the expiry but didn't notice the three different names).

**Missed:**
- Skip quietly sets up a 250 mm Klipper printer. A reader can't know this from the screen; only the code shows it.
- "· 500 credits" doesn't say the credits were just given. It read the line correctly, so for this reader it wasn't a problem.
- "OrcaSlicer's own files were not changed" is redundant. It found the line reassuring.
- The agent card doesn't say why to sign up.
- "Account · Connected" uses printer wording for an account.

So it misses things that need knowledge from outside the screen, plus finer editorial calls. It catches the cryptic phrasing that worried you.

**New questions it raised that the review didn't have:**
- What happens after the free month: will I be charged, and do I need a card? It ranked this as a reason not to sign up.
- An unlabeled × on the signed-in account card, which it was afraid would sign it out.
- How long the code lasts, and whether to check spam.
- A Back link after sign-in that might undo the sign-in.

**False alarms, which were my fault:** I mixed screenshots from different paths into one sequence, and some of them had their state set by hand. So the agent saw the email change from alex@ to new@, got asked to sign in again on Home, and watched imported printers "vanish". In real use, the cold reader needs screenshots from one consistent path.

I saved this result to memory so a later session doesn't repeat the test. Nothing in the repo has changed.

Kenneth asks you to add a design-guidelines doc that covers on-screen wording and how a screen gets designed and checked.

Background: the First-Launch Confusion Review (https://claude.ai/artifact/91wmdS3QU8UkzbPi1zog15) found that design agents write cryptic UI text. Examples: "New or existing account, same door.", "The sixth digit signs you in.", "Pick how the agent should think.", "Signed in as … · 500 credits". Today agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md has no wording rule beyond one line ("use plain language instead of slicer jargon where possible"), and no doc describes a design workflow from start to finish.

What Kenneth agreed to (his words: "ok. tell the main session to do this."):
1. Keep agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md for the visual system, unchanged in scope.
2. Add a sibling doc, e.g. agent-docs/jusprin/design-guidelines.md, holding:
   - How a screen gets designed and checked, including a cold-reader step: a fresh agent sees only the screenshot (no code, spec or chat), says what each line means and what each button will do, and any mismatch with the intent means a rewrite.
   - A wording rule: every line says what the person does or what happens to them, in a full sentence, in words a newcomer already has. Name five patterns to avoid, each with a before/after pair from the review: facts joined by a middle dot; metaphors; describing the mechanism instead of the action; internal labels like "Expert"; hinting at a consequence instead of stating it (e.g. "a generic 0.4 mm printer").
3. Point to the new doc from the AGENTS.md line that sends UI work to "Writing UI code", and from agent-docs/jusprin/README.md.

Not agreed or untested: whether an agent cold reader catches as much as a real newcomer. Suggested check before relying on it: run a fresh agent on the review's original screenshots and count how many of the 23 problems it finds. An automated lint for middle dots and jargon was floated as an optional backstop, not agreed.
</cross-session-message>

# JusPrin production documentation

This directory is the canonical starting point for production work on `jusprin-newui`. It preserves the durable product and engineering decisions from `jusprin-v2-poc` without importing the POC's temporary windows, probes, static mocks, generated evidence, or environment-gated startup paths.

Read these documents in order:

1. [Product definition](product-definition.md) — the human/agent boundary, required product surfaces, workflow, and visibility rules.
2. [Production architecture](architecture.md) — the selected native/WebView architecture, ownership rules, component boundaries, and implementation sequence.
3. [Engineering and verification method](engineering-method.md) — how to assess risk and what evidence is required before calling a feature complete.
4. [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) — known Orca behaviors, lifecycle traps, event and history constraints, and testing lessons.
5. [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md) — required before changing any OrcaSlicer-owned file: where a seam belongs, why additive beats rewritten, how to leave a conflict that resolves correctly, and what evidence a change must record.
6. [Design system](design-system.md) — brand behavior, semantic UI tokens, typography, spacing, accessibility, and asset rules.
7. [POC reference](poc-reference.md) — exact pointers to the spike-only documents, code, commits, logs, screenshots, and generated brand artifacts left on `jusprin-v2-poc`.
8. [Tool extension guide](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md) — shared Agent/MCP contracts, process-settings workflow, execution and verification requirements.
9. [Local autosave and version history](autosave-version-history.md) — managed project storage, migration, restore, export, retention, and failure behavior.

Printer UI without hardware (Bambu in-process fake; control file; isolated app): [Fake Bambu README](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md). Moonraker and OctoPrint without hardware (Docker, real host software, simulated boards): [print hosts README](../../tests/printer_hosts/README.md).

## Governing decisions

- JusPrin is an AI-piloted 3D-printing product built on OrcaSlicer, not a replacement slicing engine.
- OrcaSlicer's C++ model, slicing pipeline, viewport, geometry operations, project serialization, and undo stack remain authoritative.
- The production application stays native C++/wxWidgets/OpenGL. The Agent conversation uses a local React/TypeScript application inside `wxWebView`.
- JavaScript renders state and submits typed commands; it never owns editable Orca project state.
- When logic could live in either C++ or a React page, it goes in the page unless there is a strong reason for C++: it touches Orca state, enforces a limit or boundary the app must guarantee, has to work without a page, or needs a thread or lifetime the page lacks. See [Where logic goes](architecture.md#where-logic-goes-the-page-first).
- Product policy lives in fork-owned files. OrcaSlicer-owned files receive only small, product-neutral, additive seams — every line changed there is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase.
- The user owns physical facts, object meaning, desired outcomes, privacy and legal decisions, and starting consequential physical actions.
- The production branch must not import experimental POC behavior merely because it demonstrated feasibility. Use the POC as evidence and reimplement through stable production boundaries.

## Source lineage

`jusprin-newui` and `jusprin-v2-poc` share base commit `8500fcdcca` (`v2.4.2`). The POC reference is pinned to final POC commit `9bba835b92`, so future changes to branch names do not make the historical evidence ambiguous.

# JusPrin design system

**Status:** Canonical product and brand guidance for `jusprin-newui`.

JusPrin should make advanced 3D printing feel immediate: a confident path from model to machine that removes detours without hiding control. The product should feel focused, assured, inventive, and approachable. Its voice is direct, capable, and optimistic—never cute, cryptic, or over-engineered.

The JusPrin logo is a soft-serve cone, chosen on 2026-11-03 from the concepts on the JusPrin Logo Concepts canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/Qroq8EdcQDSPkCAyFceDtQ). It replaced the earlier star-and-ring mark, which is still in repository history at revision `6eecb78b19`. The purple gradient endpoints are the Orbit and Bloom tokens. Positioning language in the POC brand kit is proposed product direction, not an externally sourced market claim.

## Brand behavior

- **Focused:** every element earns its place.
- **Assured:** guidance is calm and actions are decisive.
- **Inventive:** the product is technical without being intimidating.
- **Approachable:** use plain language instead of slicer jargon where possible.
- Make the next action obvious. Brand behavior should feel as focused as the visual system.

The mark is a soft-serve swirl of four rounded print layers on a waffle cone, with a curl on top: 3D printing shown as something friendly. Beside it, the name is cut into the same layers (seven for capitals, five for small letters), and a small nozzle above the i is still printing its dot, the last layer. `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Brand/brand_logo.py` draws every logo file from this one geometry.

Write the name exactly as **JusPrin**: capital J and P, no space, never all caps in body copy. Use surrounding text color for the name in ordinary copy; do not force a gradient into small text.

## Logo use

The primary expressions are the horizontal lockup, the compact product mark, and the text wordmark. Use the compact mark for application icons and small product contexts.

- Clear space: at least one quarter of the mark width on every side.
- Minimum digital mark: 24 px.
- Minimum digital horizontal lockup: 120 px.
- Minimum printed mark: 8 mm.
- Minimum printed lockup: 32 mm.
- Below these sizes, use the mark alone and verify that the orbit arcs remain distinct.

## Writing UI code

Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from the design system and
from the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.

1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in
   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a
   later edit cannot silently move it, then read it from code. Do not write
   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
   value that exists in the design artifacts but not in the roles or scales is a design
   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.
4. **Pick the nearest role, never a bespoke size.** The roles are the whole
   type system. Bold at a body or label size is a role of its own; if a
   surface seems to need a size that no role has, see rule 2.
5. **The design system wins when it and the code disagree.** The two Claude
   artifacts are the source of truth (Kenneth, 2026-10-20; Figma is
   retired): the Design System
   (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) and the "JusPrin v2"
   canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). The canvas
   frozen on 2026-10-27 (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v)
   is history, not a source. Change the token file to match, or, when the
   code's value is the one to keep, change the artifact first. Do not trust
   old commit messages about either.
6. **Run the guards before calling UI work done:** `brand_tokens_tests`,
   `shell_theme_tests`, and `npm test` in `AgentUI`. Then look at the surface
   in the running app; the guards prove the code went through the tokens,
   not that the result looks right.
7. **Upstream files are off limits for style.** OrcaSlicer's own screens are
   retinted through the hooks `BrandPalette.cpp` installs and nothing else;
   see [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). Their radii and fonts stay
   OrcaSlicer's until the surface is replaced.

content.content:
## Design handoff requirements

Every high-fidelity product frame must:

1. Define each application screen in one canonical appearance mode. Do not
   create paired light and dark screen frames. The other mode must be
   deterministically derived by the design system from the same semantic token
   names, component variants, geometry, content, and interaction state. Verify
   light/dark differences in the design-system primitives and semantic mappings
   rather than duplicating every application screen.
2. State the mode, viewport, component variants, keyboard focus, and any deliberate exception.
3. Use DIP, native density, and the design system's radius scale.
4. Use HarmonyOS Sans SC for product UI, and monospace only for code (the design system's `code` style uses the system monospace font).
5. Show normal, hover, pressed, disabled, focus, error, warning, and success states as applicable.
6. Test long filenames, localized labels, dense settings, empty states, and narrow windows.
7. Use the logo files in `resources/jusprin/branding/` and the existing functional icon system.
8. Label and justify any value that is not in the token files.
9. Draw a repeated feature composition, such as the setup card, chat header, composer or printer-and-spool chip, once, on the Compositions page of the JusPrin v2 canvas, and import it into screens by name. Never paste a copy into a screen.

The POC decks, rendered examples, horizontal lockup PNG, and generation sources remain available for visual-reference work through [POC reference](poc-reference.md). They are not runtime dependencies.
----
85:- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.

Don't propose Figma changes or cite Figma." metadata: node_type: memory type: feedback originSessionId: 1ad40aa6-b204-449c-8be8-7600964a4f52 modified: 2026-10-27T20:28:20.888Z --- Kenneth, 2026-10-20: "We're not changing Figma anymore. We have migrated to Cloud artifact." The two Claude artifacts are now the design source of truth: the Design System (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) and the "JusPrin v2" canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v). They started as copies of Figma ([[jusprin-claude-design-system-artifact]]), but they are no longer re-synced from it. **Why:** design changes now happen in the artifacts, so a Figma-based argument or a "change Figma" proposal points at a dead file. **How to apply:** check designs by reading the artifact files (Artifact read with `path`, e.g. `project/-.dc.html` on the canvas); never suggest editing Figma or waiting for Figma seat allowance; when citing a design, name the artifact board, not a Figma node. Describe what the board actually draws, not what a component's internal properties imply: a menu row with no fill or border draws no shape at all, so it is not "a square row". Older memories that say "Figma is the source of truth" ([[design-token-sync-decisions]], [[figma-jusprin-v2-file]]) are superseded on that point. **Restated by Kenneth later on 2026-10-20:** "from now on, we should assume claude design artifact is the up to date design. figma is out of date." Docs changed the same day (uncommitted on jusprin-newui): agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md no longer points at Figma, and the repo skill .claude/skills/figma-agent-design is marked retired. **Also frozen (Kenneth, 2026-10-27):** the old Claude Design project "OrcaSlicer AI redesign concepts" (claude.ai/design/p/d981c5e2-…, files like `Orca Chat Panel.dc.html`). It is history for how a decision was reached, never the current design. For the chat panel, including G-code entries and print bands, the current boards are the five `main-print-timeline-panel-full*` boards on the canvas's Main Page. **The canvas moved (2026-10-27):** VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v is itself frozen ("JusPrin v2 (frozen 2026-10-27)" title, a `frozen-pointer-*` note on every page). The current canvas is https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ, with numbered board names (`main-05-print-timeline-panel-full-no-revert`, `main-07-…full`, `agent-ui-01-timeline-cards-manufacturing-history-state-matrix`) and shared parts as `` components that render.py can't draw. Check the canvas title before editing. On it (version 1793132250-e29e) `plates-26e3-project-print-history` and the state matrix were redrawn to the G-code design (matrix now 3 variants, 772 px tall). I also edited 26e3 on the frozen canvas by mistake (version 1793132033-a81d); at Kenneth's request it was restored byte-for-byte to the original BUILD 1 board in version 1793132895-0706. **How to apply:** when a memory note, commit message, doc or old plan cites a Figma frame, node id or value, treat it as history and check the artifact board instead. Edit the artifacts directly (recipe in [[jusprin-claude-design-system-artifact]]); never re-sync them from Figma, which would overwrite newer design. ### show-design-in-the-screen --- name: show-design-in-the-screen description: "Kenneth, 2026-10-28: a design board for review must show the change inside the whole screen it lives in (real viewport, the pane, the header), never a component drawn alone; he rejected header-strip-only boards as drawn 'out of thin air in the vacuum'." metadata: node_type: memory type: feedback originSessionId: 4219b55f-d6b6-4807-b23b-1c973a54c315 modified: 2026-10-28T15:41:05.547Z --- On 2026-10-28 I published four boards for the "from the file" printer-chip mark: the header strip alone, the chip's states, the menu popover, the header after a choice. Kenneth: "So you drew the mark out of the thin air in the vacuum? Where should they be attached to? … do you know how to show a design to a human being?" He was looking at the Printer & Material Settings page, where every board is a whole 1280×800 Prepare screen. **Why:** a reviewer judges a change by what surrounds it: the bed it sits over, the pane beside it, the message that follows. A strip with no screen gives nothing to attach the change to. **How to apply:** every review board is the whole screen at the app's size (1280×800 for Prepare), composed the way the canvas's existing screens are: header, viewport, Agent pane with the shared components (`comp-chat-header`, `comp-pinned-setup-card`, `comp-composer` via ``), and the timeline rows the app really showed. Use the walkthrough's real screenshots for the viewport (crop, upload as a canvas asset, ``), and the app's real strings. A component-states board may come last, as a detail, never first or alone. Builder pattern: `figma-mirror/tools/composer/build_file_printer_page.py` (second version). Related: [[canvas-boards-from-bundle-rules]], [[file-printer-switch-decisions]]. ### mockup-strings-from-real-output --- name: mockup-strings-from-real-output description: "UI sketches that summarise data must use strings a rule produced from real data, never hand-typed ideal text" metadata: node_type: memory type: feedback originSessionId: 9cbf10d8-8485-416c-81ef-f11d3e2c8b83 modified: 2026-10-08T12:57:29.751Z --- When sketching UI that summarises OrcaSlicer data (the setup summary card, 2026-10-07/08), do not hand-type ideal strings such as "Brim 8 mm outer" or a shortened preset name. Kenneth challenged exactly those: there was no rule that produces them, and measuring showed they did not fit the line either. **Why:** Kenneth said an earlier agent drew a good-looking mockup, then at implementation found no way from raw data to the "smart" summary and fell back to hard-coding a few fields (the 13-key `kSetupKeys` list). He wants that trap avoided, not repeated. **How to apply:** Before proposing a layout, write the generic rule, run it over real data (all settings, all shipped preset names), measure lengths against the real line width, and fill the sketch only from that output. Say plainly which phrasing only a model could write. He asked for a 5% random sample of the output to review, not the full table. The formatter is `Workspace/SettingDisplay.hpp`, tested by `setting_display_tests` (links libslic3r only, builds in minutes in a fresh worktree). See [[figma-dump-then-measure-parity]]. **2026-10-08 follow-up (finishing the Codex implementation, worktree `~/.codex/worktrees/setup-card-differences/JusPrin`, branch `codex/setup-card-differences`, uncommitted):** Kenneth said the other agent matched the design terribly. Its fixtures did match; what was wrong only showed in the real app and in what it deleted. Checks that found the defects, in the order worth repeating: - Restore the tests an agent deleted for behaviour the handoff said stays unchanged, then run them: this caught a saved card showing "Agent is applying…". - Pixel-diff, not eyeball: render the built fixtures into the mockup's own frame (same scaffold CSS, 320 px, light and dark), screenshot both with headless Chrome, `PIL.ImageChops.difference(...).getbbox()`. - Real app: `JusPrinShellHarness --light-ui|--dark-ui --setup-differences-capture ` edits process, filament, printer and object settings and photographs the web view. Use `capture_web_view` (WebKit snapshot); `write_screen_capture` gives blank 810-byte PNGs from a shell. - `Search::OptionsSearcher::get_option` only knows settings visible in the current user mode and returns a neighbour otherwise; `get_group_and_category(";")` (try `key#0` for per-extruder keys) is mode-independent. - `PREVIEW_OUT=... npx vitest run` with no filter lets every `*.preview.test.tsx` overwrite the same file; name the test. - Kenneth, same day: hard-coded setting names are "a big problem" wherever they are, not only on the card. The chat timeline's agent pill (`ChangeRows.tsx`) looked up "Wall loops" and infill by label; he wanted it shown with a screenshot and gone. Do not leave such code with a note; fix it and show before/after. - A live capture only proves the design if the app is in the mockup's state. Mine first showed a project with no recorded purpose, so the title and lines differed and he called it out. The harness mode now records a purpose and applies a patch through `host.tools().propose("intent_update" / "settings_apply_patch", …, )`, slices, and waits out the 60 s "Updated" window. - Landed 2026-10-08: cherry-picked onto `jusprin-newui` in the main checkout as 198c64606f (not pushed by me), after Kenneth rewrote the approval-removal history (eb45279cd5). `origin/temp/setup-card-differences` (4650dd3093) is the pre-rewrite copy. ### canvas-boards-from-bundle-rules --- name: canvas-boards-from-bundle-rules description: "Kenneth's 2026-10-21 correction: a canvas board I draw must copy the Design System bundle's CSS rules and the app's own markup, never an older board or memory; the calibration page had 14 px menu rows drawn at 13, a missing Connect… row, a black Remove, a stale reply-choice style and more." metadata: node_type: memory type: feedback originSessionId: 9ce2f3c8-7b6d-4ba7-99ce-889f9d9f192a modified: 2026-10-22T00:09:35.890Z --- Kenneth, 2026-10-21, on the calibration page I drew: "It looks like you didn't follow this hygiene. read design guidelines in readme, and fix your own sloppiness", then "I suspect there were more sloppiness in the boards you designed". He was right on both counts. I had copied markup from older canvas boards (the printer-menu board at 13 px rows, the stale ds-chat-reply-choice board) and from memory (a Home kebab with no Connect…, a black Remove, a 220 px width, the filament menu in an old order), instead of from the two sources that are authoritative. **Why:** rule 5 of "Writing UI code" (agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md) says the design system wins, and the design system's truth is its coded bundle (`figma-mirror/published/ds/project/components/bundle.css`, classes `.jp-*`), not any one board on the canvas: boards drift (the printer-menu board draws rows at 13 px, the reply choice board draws the pre-capsule style). For surfaces the bundle has no component for (the printer receipt, a sent photo in a message), the app's own CSS and TSX are the source. **How to apply:** before drawing a board, dump the bundle rules for every component used (`grep '\.jp-' bundle.css`) and read the app's row set for every menu (Shell/PrinterMenu.cpp, Shell/FilamentMenu.cpp, HomeUI PrinterMenu.tsx) and the app's CSS for chat pieces (AgentUI/styles.css). Also wrong the first time: the chat header named the project where the app names the chat (3 to 7 words, kConversationTitleInstructions); the pinned card was the stale "CURRENT SETUP · See all" board, not the app's Setup summary (`.current-setup*`: label + state header in Metadata Bold, purpose as Body Bold title, presets line, plan headline, Label Bold metrics with 14 px glyphs, hairline, All settings link; out of date drops the accent and uses the attention block); the composer placeholder was not the approved board's. Draw rows at Body 14 / 36 px (`.jp-menu-row`), popovers on surface-raised 280 wide, reply choices as capsules on surface-subtle, user bubbles 10/12 padding radius-medium at 75% width, tool cards on surface-subtle, project cards 293 wide with one status line, and no annotation tags ("NEW") inside a drawn component. State in the caption which rows are new. Known DS-vs-canvas inconsistency not mine to settle: `.jp-bubble-agent` has an avatar; the app and the timeline boards draw agent prose without one. Related: [[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]], [[jusprin-claude-design-system-artifact]], [[calibration-design-decisions]]. Since 2026-10-20 these artifacts ARE the source of truth ([[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]]); edit them directly. The Figma re-sync steps below are history. 1. Design System: https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL (version 9) - `tokens.json` + `tokens.css`, 37 coded React components (`window.JusPrin`). - Each component card: every variant Figma draws, a Light and a Dark panel, then the coded component. Design canvas "JusPrin v2": https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v (version 7): 10 pages with Figma's names in Figma's order, 198 artboards at their Figma x,y and in Figma's layer order, each drawn in the Light or Dark mode Figma sets on it; "… · Light & Dark" review frames are drawn whole.
